attracted the level of media attention that might indicate the award's national or international
recognition. Moreover, it has not submitted information about the individuals who participated in the
events, including their caliber and skill level, which might reveal the prestige and recognition of the
competition. A competition may be open to individuals from throughout a particular country or
countries, but this factor alone is not adequate to establish that an award or prize is "nationally or
internationally recognized." The burden is on the Petitioner to demonstrate the level of recognition
and achievement associated with the Beneficiary's awards. Finally, although in its appeal brief the
Petitioner provides information about NAGA and CBJJE, it did not submit any corroborating evidence
to support its claims.
Accordingly, the Petitioner did not demonstrate that the Beneficiary satisfies this criterion.

Published material in professional or major trade publications or other major media
about the alien, relating to the alien's work in the field for which classification is
sought, which shall include the title, date, and author ofs uch published material, and
any necessary translation. 8 C.F.R. § 214.2(o)(3)(iii)(B)(3).
The Petitioner provided a copy of an article from an unknown Spanish-language newspaper and
screenshots of an article from an unknown blog that do not comply with the regulation at 8 C.F.R.
§ 103.2(b)(3) requiring "a foll English language translation." Because the Petitioner did not submit a
complete translation of these items, it did not demonstrate that the articles are published material about
the Beneficiary relating to his work. In addition, the Petitioner did not include the required title, date,
and author of the material. Further, the Petitioner did not present evidence establishing that those
sources are each a professional or major trade publication or other major medium.
Accordingly, the Petitioner did not show that the Beneficiary meets this criterion.

The scope of this evidentiary criterion focuses on the Beneficiary and the relative importance of his
position within the organizations that have employed him. The record does not contain evidence that
would establish that the Beneficiary's position with the petitioning organization was in a critical or
essential capacity, such as evidence establishing how the Beneficiary's instructor position related to other
instructor positions in the organization, the number of coaches employed, or how many of the coaches
took athletes to national events. The evidence submitted does not clearly show the Beneficiary's
established successful history of instructing top-level athletes. Further, the evidence does not establish
that the Petitioner has a distinguished reputation in the sport of MMA. Based on the forgoing, the
Petitioner has not established that the Beneficiary satisfies this criterion.
